content.title: About
content.content: A bagel is a ring‑shaped yeast‑leavened bread that is boiled briefly before being baked to a golden crust. This version incorporates pieces of fruit (other than raisins), giving it a subtle sweetness and a burst of flavor.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The classic bagel originated in Eastern European Jewish communities in the 19th century.
Bagels are typically boiled in water with a touch of baking soda or honey, which creates their characteristic glossy crust.
Fruit‑filled bagels are popular in the United States and Canada, using apples, cranberries, cherries and other berries.
Bagels are denser than regular bread because of the double cooking process of boiling and baking.
Japan has a similar product called “pankē,” but with a softer texture.

items.title: Source of complex carbs
items.content: Bagels provide sustained energy thanks to slowly digestible carbohydrates.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Whole‑wheat dough supplies thiamine, niacin and folate, important for metabolism.

items.title: Fruit antioxidants
items.content: The added fruit contributes vitamin C, polyphenols and other antioxidants that support immunity.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Whole‑grain flour and fruit pieces increase fiber content, promoting healthy digestion.

items.title: Low in trans fats
items.content: Traditional bagel preparation does not involve hydrogenated oils.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bagels contain wheat, making them unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Because of the dense structure and fruit sugars, bagels can raise blood glucose quickly.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit additions increase total sugar, which should be considered by individuals with diabetes.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Bagels are more calorie‑dense than regular bread, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Slice the bagel in half and spread cream cheese, nut butter or hummus. It pairs well with yogurt, cottage cheese, or as a sandwich with smoked salmon or deli meat. Lightly toasting before serving adds a crunchy crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep bagels in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days. For longer storage, refrigerate (up to 7 days) or freeze (up to 3 months). Warm in a toaster or oven before eating.
